query: What government data sources exist as alternatives or complements to NFIP claims data for measuring flood damage at the ZCTA level in the United States?
sub_questions: FEMA Individual Assistance (IA) via OpenFEMA -- volume, spatial resolution, API access, fields, biases
SBA Disaster Loans -- spatial resolution, format, creditworthiness bias, coverage
USGS Short-Term Network (STN) High Water Marks -- event count, spatial density, suitability as ZCTA target
NOAA Storm Events Database -- granularity, reliability, known issues
HUD CDBG-DR allocations -- granularity, reporting standards
Any other federal/state data sources that provide flood damage or impact at sub-county resolution
confidence: HIGH for source identification, MEDIUM for bias assessment
gaps: SBA disaster loan data portal returned 500 errors; ZIP-level fields unverified
HUD CDBG-DR QPR spatial resolution unverified (site blocked)
SHELDUS database access and fields unverified (site blocked)
USGS STN HWM field schema not retrieved (API returned empty for all tested events)
State-level damage assessment databases (FL, TX, NC, LA) not investigated
FEMA Preliminary Damage Assessment data availability not confirmed
Census Post-Disaster Household Pulse Survey spatial resolution unverified
NOAA Storm Events format documentation PDF was blocked; fields verified via direct CSV download instead
key_findings: FEMA IA registrations (6.4M records) at ZIP/census-block level is the strongest NFIP alternative
USACE NSI provides per-structure exposure data with flood zones and replacement values
NOAA Storm Events is county/zone level -- too coarse for ZCTA targets
USGS STN HWMs are too sparse for ZCTA target variables but excellent for model validation
HUD CDBG-DR is derivative of FEMA/SBA data and typically grantee-level resolution
No single source captures total flood damage; multi-source fusion is required
